messages.author: 43e2e19dd6bd2992
messages.subject: getting number of pm probes
parts:
Hi,
I want to get the number of probes per group. I know there is a
function in affxparser 'readCdfNbrOfCellsPerUnitGroup' that will give
me the number of cells per group. My question is if I just want the
number of PM probes. With readUnits, there is an option 'stratifyBy =
"pm"'; so I could just calculate the probes manually. Is there a
function that does this already?
Thanks,
Elizabeth

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] getting number of pm probes
parts:
Hi,

unfortunately I don't think there is such a function in affxparser.
Best is to use readUnits() and scan the list yourself as you suggest.
You may want to write a wrapper method for this that could be added to
the AffymetrixCdfFile class. Whenever affxparser supports the same,
we can just update the internal code.

FYI: It has been a long-term plan/wish to add the 'stratifyBy'
argument to all affxparser method where applicable. It has also been
my hope to move it all into the C code which would speed up things
*substantially* (all the 'stratifyBy' code is now in R and there is a
large overhead in doing this). However, since things work as is, it
never made it to my top-10 list of most-important things todo. It is
still down there around 10-20...

Cheers

Henrik

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: getting number of pm probes
parts:
Hi.

You can replace all "$" calls with .subset2() calls to avoid the
overhead of method dispatching. It is also much faster to make use of
'use.names=FALSE' in unlist(). Something like this:

cellList0 <- getCellIndices(cdf, units=99:102, stratifyBy="pm");

groupSizes <- lapply(cellList0, FUN=function(unit) {
groups <- .subset2(unit, "groups");
groups <- lapply(groups, FUN=function(group) {
length(.subset2(group, "indices"));
})
groups <- unlist(groups, use.names=FALSE);
groups;
})

Since getCellIndices() returns only one item per unit and also per
group, that is, we can replace "groups" with 1, and also "indices"
with 1, which is probably faster.

The following might also speed up things, I'm not sure:

# a) First, move things up in the tree
cellList <- lapply(cellList0, FUN=function(unit) {
groups <- .subset2(unit, 1);
groups <- lapply(groups, FUN=function(group) {
.subset2(group, 1);
})
groups;
})

# a) Same but faster
cellList <- lapply(cellList0, FUN=function(unit) {
groups <- .subset2(unit, 1);
lapply(groups, FUN=.subset2, 1);
})

# a) Same but faster again
cellList <- lapply(cellList0, FUN=function(unit) {
lapply(.subset2(unit, 1), FUN=.subset2, 1);
})

# b) count from the above
groupSizes <- lapply(cellList, FUN=lapply, length);
groupSizes <- lapply(groupSizes, FUN=unlist, use.names=FALSE);

The you might also want to replace every lapply() with an internal
call to .Internal(lapply, FUN), see print(lapply).

If you do some benchmarking with system.time() or similar let us know
how it goes.

Hope this helps

Henrik
